what: The Instagram Caption Generator gives you ten caption ideas at a time for 13 topics, including travel, food, fitness, fashion, beauty, business, photography, pets, nature, family, gaming and art, in six moods: happy, motivational, funny, aesthetic, loving and professional.

Type what your post is about, such as a city or a dish, and it is worked into the captions. Choose how many emojis and hashtags to add (up to 5, the most Instagram allows) and whether to end with a question for comments or a save-and-share reminder. Each idea shows its character count against Instagram's 2,200 limit.
The Bio tab makes short profile bios from your role, location and call to action, sized for Instagram's 150-character limit. Everything is made on your device from a built-in template library.
uses: Find a caption fast when you have the photo but not the words.
Write professional captions with a call to action.
Add the place or dish and get matching hashtags.
Write a clear bio with your role, location and link prompt.
Generate a batch of ideas for the week ahead.
tutorial: Use the tabs at the top.
The topic sets the emojis and hashtags; the mood sets the tone of the words.
Type a word or two, such as "Lisbon" or "pasta night". It also becomes your first hashtag.
Choose none, a few or lots of emojis, 0 to 5 hashtags and the ending.
Press Generate for ten new ideas.
Tap Copy under the one you like and paste it into Instagram.
features: Captions are built around your topic.
Up to 5, the most Instagram allows on a post, starting with your own keyword.
Every idea checked against Instagram's limits.

example.title: Worked example: a travel post
example.text: Choose Travel, the Happy mood and type "Lisbon". Set A few emojis, 5 hashtags and "A question for comments". One idea reads: "Making memories with Lisbon. ✨ Which one is your favourite? 👇" followed by #lisbon #travelgram #wanderlust and two more. Tap Copy and paste it under your photo.

tips: Put the most interesting words in the first line; that is what people see first.
Mix popular and specific hashtags, and only use ones that match the post.
End with a question to get more comments.
Edit the idea a little so it sounds like you.
problems: Press Generate again, or change the mood or topic for fresh templates.
My bio is marked too long
Shorten the name or call to action, or choose fewer emojis.
Hashtags do not match my post
Pick the closest topic and type a specific word in "About"; it becomes the first hashtag.
